title: Can a correct key survive skipped draws?
question: Under the pinned key-skip simulation, can a skip-aware decoder recover a planted correct key as the text grows to full LP2 length?
reader_question: Could key skipping make a correct key look wrong?
summary: In a source-backed plant-and-recover test, rigid alignment fails quickly while the skip-aware beam retains a planted correct key through 12,956 runes. This checks decoder power under a synthetic model, not a real LP2 key.
finding: At 400 runes, rigid detection succeeds in 1/200 plants and the beam in 200/200. At 12,956 runes, all three beam plants pass the fixed score and 90% recovery gates; mean rune recovery is 99.97%. The full-length wrong-key control scores -7.30 below the -5.5 reading threshold. All non-timing source fields replay exactly after F0 parity passes 24 cases.
limitations: The source uses one KJV-derived synthetic plaintext, a known SHA-256-counter key, and a filter probability fitted to LP2 repeat scarcity. This verifies the decoder under that plant, not the presence of that filter or key in LP2; its score bar is not calibrated as a family-wide search threshold.
next_steps: Any LP2 claim needs a fixed candidate key and filter rule that predicts unseen manuscript text under held-out controls.

scope.representation: 12,956-rune synthetic GP29 ciphertext built from the pinned KJV source text and SHA-256-counter key; LP2 contributes only the previously measured repeat-rate calibration.
scope.procedure: Replay source F0 reference-versus-fast-beam gate, B1 200 drift samples, B2 six lengths × 200 planted windows, B3 six lengths × three planted keys plus one wrong-key full-length control; compare all non-timing source fields.
scope.parameters: Source revision f08b20b; suppression 0.8129; beam width 400; maximum three skipped draws per step; reading score gate -5.5 and minimum planted rune recovery 90%.
scope.exclusions: Real LP2 key search, other language/key/filter families, independent held-out classifier power, source B.4 ladder and later R18 subattacks.

review.reviewer: F0 parity gate, exact source-field replay and independent drift/bound arithmetic check

reproduction.environment: Python 3.9+ and NumPy, pinned Dukotah checkout at f08b20b and exact KJV source bytes. Runner stages all hashed dependencies in a temporary tree.

visuals.caption: Detection of a planted correct key by rigid alignment versus a skip-aware beam; full-length recovery below.
